content.text:
Yes, it looks stuck. Nothing is moving through the queue.

- **Nothing is queued.** GitHub's native merge queue isn't enabled on this repo. The merge queue here is Trunk's, and none of the 16 open PRs has been picked up.
- **Every open PR has the `trunk-not-ready` label.** Each one shows `BLOCKED` with no review decision. #108 is `DIRTY`, so it also has a merge conflict.
- **The `pullfrog` check is failing on the PRs I looked at.** I checked #229, #225 and #224. Their other checks pass (Tests, Trunk Check, Docs & Assets, Entire Gates). The #224 run took 19m44s. Its failed-step log shows only post-job git cleanup, so I haven't found the actual error.

The likely cause is that `trunk-not-ready` is only removed once `pullfrog` passes or approves, and `pullfrog` is failing. I haven't confirmed that. I couldn't find the label's rules in the repo, because my grep errored out (a zsh glob problem). The recent commit "Stop docs claiming the merge queue waits on pullfrog-approval" suggests that link may be less direct than it looks.

I can pull the full `pullfrog` run log to find the real error. I can also look for where `trunk-not-ready` gets applied and removed. Which do you want?

content.text:
Yes, it's stuck. The Trunk bot comments confirm that PRs #229, #225, #224, #196 and #104 were submitted to Trunk Merge. They're all waiting in `trunk-not-ready` for the branch protection rules to pass, and none has been admitted to the queue.

**Cause:** `main` requires four status checks: Trunk Check, Tests, Generate & Verify Docs and Social Cards, and `pullfrog-approval`.
- The first three pass on the PRs I checked.
- `pullfrog-approval` is not in any PR's check list. The only pullfrog check is called `pullfrog`, and it fails.
- Because the required check is never reported, branch protection stays `BLOCKED`. Trunk waits on that, so nothing is admitted.

**Not confirmed:** I only inspected the PR comments and the branch rules. I didn't open the Trunk dashboard, so I can't see the queue's own state. The `trunk` CLI doesn't expose merge queue status.

The repo's own docs recently changed (commit `9e1291e`, "Stop docs claiming the merge queue waits on pullfrog-approval"). That suggests `pullfrog-approval` was meant to be dropped from the required checks, but the ruleset still lists it.

**Likely fixes** (both need repo admin, so I haven't touched them):
1. Remove `pullfrog-approval` from the `main` ruleset's required checks. This unblocks everything, if the docs change reflects the intended design.
2. Or fix the `pullfrog` workflow so it reports a check named `pullfrog-approval` and passes.

Want me to look at the pullfrog workflow in `.github/workflows` to see which of the two matches the intent?

result.output:
Graph mode adds one more admission gate beyond `merge.required_statuses`: the
queue holds every PR at Not Ready until impacted targets have been uploaded
for its head sha. `.github/workflows/trunk-impacted-targets.yml` uploads them
on every PR to main (`PUT /v2/impacted-targets` authorized by the
`TRUNK_API_TOKEN` repo secret). The job stays out of
`merge.required_statuses` on purpose — the queue waits on the upload itself,
not the check — but a red `Upload Impacted Targets` job means nothing was
uploaded, and PRs stall at Not Ready even with every required status green.

`pullfrog-approval` (Pullfrog's AI review verdict) is required on the GitHub
side only (ruleset `main - PR requirements` plus classic branch protection on
`main`, pinned to the Pullfrog app). It is deliberately not in
`merge.required_statuses`, so the Trunk queue does not wait on it.

The five PRs I confirmed were submitted to Trunk Merge and are stuck:

- https://github.com/elviskahoro/buridan-ui/pull/229
- https://github.com/elviskahoro/buridan-ui/pull/225
- https://github.com/elviskahoro/buridan-ui/pull/224
- https://github.com/elviskahoro/buridan-ui/pull/196
- https://github.com/elviskahoro/buridan-ui/pull/104

The other 11 open PRs also carry `trunk-not-ready` and show `BLOCKED`, but I didn't check their comments to see if they were submitted. They are #195, #193, #192, #187, #186, #183, #180, #178, #115, #108 (which also has a merge conflict) and #105.

**Root cause, from the #224 pullfrog log:**
- The Pullfrog review agent runs on `fireworks-ai/.../glm-5p3`.
- The model goes silent: "no opencode events for 902s", then "the provider never returned a first token".
- The action fails with `activity timeout`, so Pullfrog never posts the `pullfrog-approval` verdict.
- `main` requires `pullfrog-approval`, so every PR stays `BLOCKED` and Trunk never admits it.

**The fix is in `.github/workflows/pullfrog.yml`:** switch the `model:` line to a provider that responds. I haven't edited it yet, for two reasons:
- `gh secret list` returned nothing usable, so I can't tell which provider keys exist. If I pick a model whose key is missing, it will fail the same way.
- The file is marked "DO NOT EDIT EXCEPT WHERE INDICATED", and the `model:` line is the only part meant to change.

Which provider should I switch to? Anthropic is the obvious candidate, via `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, if either is set. Or if you'd rather unblock the queue right now, you can remove `pullfrog-approval` from the `main` ruleset (admin only).

After the change merges, the PRs need a Pullfrog re-run, or a push, to get a fresh verdict. I can trigger that for you.

content.text:
Yes, I think the model is wrong, and the evidence points to two problems.

**What it's set to**

`.github/workflows/pullfrog.yml` has `fireworks-ai/accounts/fireworks/models/glm-5p3`. The run log says `"…glm-5p3" is not a curated alias — passing through as a raw model specifier`. So Pullfrog didn't recognise the ID and passed it to OpenCode as-is.

**What's off**

1. **Wrong model name.** The workflow comment says it matches roborev's model. Every `.roborev.toml` in your repos, including this one, uses `glm-5p3-flash`, not `glm-5p3`. Plain `glm-5p3` may not exist, or may not be served on Fireworks serverless. That would explain why the provider never returned a first token.
2. **Different provider prefix.** roborev uses `fireworks/accounts/...`, and the flox-conductor-sandbox config says that prefix is required. Pullfrog uses `fireworks-ai/accounts/...`. That prefix may be correct for models.dev, though. I can't tell which one OpenCode wants.

**Possible fix**

The smallest change is `glm-5p3` → `glm-5p3-flash`, keeping the `fireworks-ai/` prefix.

A `Pullfrog` workflow_dispatch run finished successfully about an hour ago (run 41353637368, "Review new commits on #189"). I haven't looked at which model it used. If it's the same `glm-5p3` line, then the model name probably isn't the whole story. It could be that Fireworks was only intermittently unresponsive.

Want me to look at that successful run's log first, then make the `-flash` change and test it with a dispatch? That tells us whether `-flash` helps instead of guessing.
